summary: Bayfield County, WI steel tower built 1932; sources disagree on condition (standing, abandoned, decommissioned), and a trail hike still reaches it on foot.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree: the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it standing, Forest Lookouts marks it abandoned, and a trail group calls it decommissioned. The last record of its structure is a 1995 survey that found it not demolished.

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot: a 5.5-mile out-and-back hike from a County Road D parking lot about 5.2 miles south of Grand View, per a North Country Trail Association listing. The listing describes a climb to the tower, a short break there, and a return to the lot. No source says the cab is open to visitors.

corrections.why: 44 is the start of the location code 44-6W-12 (township 44, range 6 West, section 12), not an agency. No source found names the owner.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it standing and the 1995 Wisconsin Historical Society survey found it not demolished. Forest Lookouts calls it abandoned, and the North Country Trail listing calls it decommissioned. We keep standing and flag the disagreement in status_note.

notes_for_editor: Identity is solid: the WHS record, Forest Lookouts, FFLA and OSM all describe the same Bayfield County tower with the 1932 build year. Condition is the open question. The brief's standing status rests on the FFLA list, which conflicts with Forest Lookouts (abandoned). The NCTA event page text I read has no visible date, so treat it as a listing rather than proof of a recent visit. Does not say whether climbing is permitted. The brief's agency '44' is a location fragment, corrected to unknown. No fire, staffing or photo evidence found. One WebSearch pair used (two searches total for this tower).
